the social license to operate is granted to a mining company when it has a strong commitment to community development, it has a deep understanding of local socioeconomic environment, it is actively present in the region, and it effectively communicates with the community.

the factors that influence a company's ability to gain the support of the community include the company's understanding of the socioeconomic situation, the level of trust between the company and the community, and a strong commitment from the company to provide benefits to the community.

a deep understanding of a company's socioeconomic environment, a firm commitment to the community and an effective presence of Government, are the three essential factors for the provision of social license to operate in Peru.

how mining companies can improve their social performance in Peru.
the identification of the factors that influence the social license to operate of the Peruvian mining industry.
how mining companies can achieve social legitimacy and, therefore, a social license to continue their activities.

a social license to operation in Peru's mining industry is achieved through the implementation of a social responsibility policy.
a social license to mine is the result of an effective communication between all the actors involved in the mining industry.

social license to operate is not an end in itself but a means to achieve a more sustainable relationship between mining companies and local communities.
mining companies need to understand the local context and develop a strong commitment to local communities, while at the same time maintaining an effective communication with the local government.
a social license to mine can be achieved when mining companies have the support of all the stakeholders involved in the mining process, including Government and local communities.

the social license to operate is not an automatic outcome of a company's actions, and that the Government plays an essential role in this process.
